# GeoGrounding

> GeoGrounding is a structured geographic and cultural context layer for AI-powered applications — machine-readable context about a user's location (linguistic, cultural, commercial environment) that an AI can use to adapt a digital experience, not a general-purpose knowledge base or geographic database. Every statistic is tied to an authoritative source, every intentional data gap is documented rather than guessed.

Data lives under `data/` as YAML validated against JSON Schema in `schema/`. Coverage is currently partial (4 of 249 ISO 3166-1 entries curated as reference implementations).

## Core

- [README.md](README.md): quick orientation — structure, example entries, how to consume the data
- [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md): full design rationale — country/region model, IP geolocation mapping, season calendar, language modeling, sourcing rules
- [VERSIONING.md](VERSIONING.md): what a version number means (schema compatibility, not content volume), which changes are breaking, how to pin a reference for reproducibility vs. freshness
- [schema/country.schema.json](schema/country.schema.json): country-level fields (languages, ethnic groups, timezones, regions)
- [schema/region.schema.json](schema/region.schema.json): region-level fields (climate, landmarks, cuisine, sports, religion, seasonal content)
- [schema/language.schema.json](schema/language.schema.json): global per-language reference (name, basic phrases)

## Examples

- [usage_examples/python/get_data_by_ip.py](usage_examples/python/get_data_by_ip.py): reference implementation — IP-derived location + current date → the relevant region file and its currently-applicable content
